cycles.name: Foundation Forge
focuses: Build baseline strength in compound lifts and establish progressive core overload.
Ingrain movement quality, lock in training habits, and initiate a sustainable caloric deficit.

cycles.name: Volume Engine
cycles.tagline: More Work. Less Rest. Real Growth.
focuses: Increase hypertrophy volume per muscle group with higher training density and shorter rest periods.
Advance core loading from bodyweight to stability-based variations and introduce structured conditioning blocks.

cycles.name: Metabolic Override
focuses: Shift training toward high-density supersets and circuit-based resistance work to maximise energy expenditure while preserving muscle.
Peak direct abdominal volume and introduce advanced anti-extension progressions.

paragraphs: Cycle 2 did its job: bench up 25%, shoulder press up 21%, and three straight perfect weeks to finish. You're stronger and you've proven you can handle density. But the scale didn't move — and the goal was never just to be a bigger 88 kg. Cycle 3 is where that changes.

Metabolic Override turns the volume you built into fuel. Every session now runs on supersets — two exercises back to back, short rests, no dead time. The weights come down slightly and the pace goes up; that's not a compromise, it's the design. You'll burn more, keep every gram of muscle, and your conditioning finishers get sharper teeth.
Your job: respect the rest clock, log every set, and let the nutrition finally match the training. This is the cycle where the work becomes visible.
outcomes: Weekly weight average trending down 0.3–0.5 kg
Every superset completed inside the prescribed rest — no clock-stretching
Lat pulldown moving again after a six-week plateau
Pain-free lower body all cycle, split squat depth growing week by week
12 direct ab sets per week handled — your highest core dose yet
Conditioning circuit at 4 rounds feeling routine by week 5

cycles.name: Strength Reclaim
focuses: Restore and surpass Cycle 1 strength levels with reduced volume and higher intensity to protect lean mass through the deepening deficit.
Reduce conditioning volume, refine muscular detail through isolation and contraction-focused work.

paragraphs: Cycle 3 gave you the biggest strength jump you have had with me. Hack squat up 50 percent, shoulder press up 27, and the lat pulldown finally moved after sitting still for six weeks. You told me you feel stronger and you gained muscle. You are right, and the numbers back you up.

The scale went the other way and we both know why now. The doctor took your protein powder away, and getting enough protein from food alone while eating less is genuinely hard. So you ate more to cover it. The last two weeks you pulled the calories back and dropped 2 kg. Good. That is the version that works.

Strength Reclaim is heavy and short. Long rests, low reps, fewer exercises per session. Heavy weight is the strongest signal you can send your body to hold on to muscle while the food is low. You are on the barbell bench for the first time because your form has earned it. And your fat loss comes from the walking now, not from circuits you hate.
outcomes: Weigh yourself every week, same morning, same conditions, and send me the number
Barbell bench press logged, filmed once, and climbing by week 3
Hack squat starting at 50 kg and going up from there
Knee stays quiet all the way through the loaded split squats
Blood test booked and the results back to me
Incline walks on the days you are not lifting

cycles.name: The Reveal
focuses: Maintain peak strength, reduce fatigue accumulation, and bring body composition to target condition.
Transition to a maintenance caloric intake; stress-test the physique and habits that will sustain results long-term.

paragraphs: Cycle 5 is where you find out what all of this was for. The strength stays, the food gets set at a level you can live on, and the shape underneath finally shows up.
Same weight on the bar. A lot less of you around it.

days.completionMessage: That is the most weight your legs have moved in this programme. Six reps is a different job to fifteen and you handled it. Get your protein in tonight, that is what turns this into muscle you keep.

good: Keep an easy pace you could hold a conversation at
Legs should feel warm and loose, never tired
bad: Don't turn this into a workout, it is a warm-up

good: Push the floor away through your heels and lift the hips high
Feel the glutes doing the lifting, not the lower back
bad: Don't arch your back at the top to get higher

good: Sit straight down between your feet and keep the chest tall
Feel the quads and hips loading evenly
bad: Don't let the knees cave in on the way up

exercises.name: Machine Hack Squat

good: Drive the platform away through the middle of your foot
Feel the quads take the load all the way down and up
bad: Don't cut the depth short to add weight

exercises.note: Start at 50 kg. Last cycle you sat on 35 kg for three weeks and it was too light, so we are not letting you pick low on this one. Take the three seconds coming down, that slow part is where the work is.

good: Push the platform away evenly through both feet
Feel the quads and glutes working together
bad: Don't lock the knees out hard at the top

good: Kick the pad up until your legs are straight
Squeeze the quad hard for a second at the top
bad: Don't swing the weight up with your hips

good: Push all the way up onto your toes
Feel a full stretch at the bottom and a hard squeeze at the top
bad: Don't bounce out of the bottom

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout

good: Roll out only as far as you can go without your back sagging
Feel the abs fighting to stop your hips dropping
bad: Don't let your lower back arch, stop short instead

exercises.note: This is the step up from the body saw you did last cycle. Start on your knees and only go as far out as you can keep your back flat. Short and clean beats long and sloppy.

days.completionMessage: Four big lifts, long rests, no messing about. This is what a strength day feels like. Send me a video of your bench top set this week so I can see it.

good: Easy pace, just get the blood moving
Body should feel warm, not tired
bad: Don't push the pace here

good: Pull the band apart until it touches your chest
Feel the muscles between your shoulder blades switch on
bad: Don't shrug your shoulders up to your ears

good: Take the band over your head and behind you with straight arms
Feel the front of the shoulders and chest open up
bad: Don't bend the elbows to cheat the range

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press

good: Push the bar up and slightly back toward your face
Feel the chest stretch at the bottom then drive the bar up
bad: Don't bounce the bar off your chest

exercises.note: First time on the bar for you. Set the safety pins before you start, every set, no exceptions when you train alone. Around 60 kg should land near the right effort based on what you were doing with the 22 kg dumbbells. Send me a video of your top set.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown

good: Pull your elbows down toward your back pockets
Feel the lats do the pulling, not the arms
bad: Don't lean back and use your bodyweight to drag it down

exercises.note: Same grip that broke your plateau, but now heavier for 8 instead of 12. You went 43 to 52 kg last cycle. Keep it climbing.

good: Press the handles straight up until the arms are long
Feel the shoulders taking the work through the whole press
bad: Don't let your lower back arch off the pad

exercises.name: Machine Plate-Loaded Row

good: Drive your elbows back past your ribs
Squeeze the mid-back hard at the end of every rep
bad: Don't yank the weight with your lower back

exercises.note: This replaces the chest-supported dumbbell row. Same job, but the plates go up in small steps so you can actually add weight. That row sat on 16 kg for five sessions last cycle because the dumbbells jumped too big.

good: Press the handles up and slightly in toward each other
Feel the upper chest take the work, just under the collarbone
bad: Don't let the elbows flare straight out to the sides

days.completionMessage: Hamstrings and glutes got a real session today, and your knee got its first loaded single-leg work since July. Tell me how the knee feels tomorrow, not just today.

good: Easy pace to warm the hips and legs
Legs warm and ready, not fatigued
bad: Don't rush straight to the bar

good: Push through the heels and squeeze the glutes at the top
Feel the glutes switch on before you load them
bad: Don't push the hips up using your lower back

good: Drop the back knee straight down toward the floor
Feel the front leg take the work
bad: Don't let the front knee wobble side to side

exercises.name: Barbell Hip Thrust

good: Drive the hips up until your body is flat like a table
Squeeze the glutes hard at the top of every rep
bad: Don't arch your back to get higher, use the glutes

exercises.note: New lift for you and it is going to become one of your best. Start light for the first set to find the bar position on your hips, then load it up. Use a pad.

good: Curl the pad all the way to your backside
Feel the hamstrings shorten hard at the top
bad: Don't let your hips lift off the bench

exercises.name: Dumbbell Split Squat

good: Drop straight down and drive straight back up through the front heel
Feel the front quad and glute working
bad: Don't push off the back foot to help

exercises.note: Your knee is clear so single-leg work comes back, but carefully. Both feet stay on the floor, this is not the Bulgarian version that hurt you in July. Keep it at an easy effort for the first two weeks and tell me if anything sharpens up.

exercises.name: 45° Back Extension

good: Push your hips into the pad and come up until your body is straight
Feel the glutes and hamstrings pull you up
bad: Don't hyperextend and lean back past straight

exercises.note: Heavier plate than last cycle. You held 10 kg for fifteen reps, now it is ten reps with more weight against your chest.

good: Push all the way up onto the toes of the working foot
Feel the calf stretch fully at the bottom before you drive up
bad: Don't lean on the support and take the weight off the working leg

exercises.name: Side Plank

good: Push the floor away and keep your hips stacked and high
Feel the side of your trunk holding you up
bad: Don't let the hips sag toward the floor

exercises.note: Once 30 seconds a side feels easy, rest a small plate or a dumbbell on your top hip.

days.focusTag: Detail Work And A Long Walk
days.completionMessage: This is the day that shapes what the heavy days built. And the walk is doing more for the scale than any circuit ever did. Easy pace, long enough to be boring, that is the point.

good: Easy pace to warm up the shoulders and back
Warm and loose
bad: Don't skip it just because today is lighter

good: Keep the elbow pinned to your side and rotate the hand out
Feel the back of the shoulder working
bad: Don't let the elbow drift away from your body

good: Pull the band apart until it touches your chest
Feel the muscles between your shoulder blades switch on
bad: Don't shrug your shoulders up to your ears

good: Bring the handles together in front of your chest
Squeeze the chest hard for a second where the hands meet
bad: Don't let the arms bend and turn it into a press

exercises.name: Leaning Cable Lateral Raise

good: Hold the upright and lean away, then raise the arm out to shoulder height
Feel the side of the shoulder burn through the whole range
bad: Don't swing your body to throw the weight up

exercises.note: Leaning away puts the side delt under tension right from the bottom, which a normal cable raise does not. It will feel harder with less weight. That is correct.

good: Open the arms wide and back like you are opening a door
Feel the rear shoulders and upper back squeeze
bad: Don't shrug or use your lower back to swing it

exercises.name: Arm Superset

good: Curl the bar up while keeping the elbows pinned at your sides
Feel the biceps do all of the work
bad: Don't swing your body to start the rep

good: Straighten the arms fully overhead
Feel the stretch behind the arm at the bottom
bad: Don't let the elbows flare out wide

exercises.note: Curl then straight into the extension, then rest once. One rest per round, not one after each exercise.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise

good: Lift your legs up until they are straight out in front of you
Feel the lower abs curl your hips up
bad: Don't swing back and forth to get the legs up

exercises.note: Step up from the knee raises. Legs straight now. If you start swinging, bend the knees a little and keep it strict.

exercises.name: Incline Treadmill Walk

good: Set a steep incline and walk at a pace you could talk at
Legs working, breathing easy, never out of breath
bad: Don't hold the handrails, it takes all the work out of it

exercises.note: This replaces the bike intervals and the circuit. You do not like conditioning so I am not going to fight you on it. This is easy walking and it is where your fat loss comes from. Do it here, and on any day you are not in the gym.

cards.title: Protein Is the Whole Problem
cards.body:
This is the one thing standing between you and the goal, and it is not training. Without the shake you have to get it from food, and you found out how hard that is while eating less.

  • Aim for around 180 g a day, spread across your meals, not all at dinner.
  • Go for the lean stuff so the calories stay low: chicken breast, white fish, egg whites, low-fat yoghurt, cottage cheese, lean mince.
  • Build every meal around the protein first, then add the rest.

Ask your doctor whether it is whey specifically that is out or all protein supplements. That answer changes what you are allowed to eat and it is worth asking properly.

cards.title: Book the Blood Test
cards.body:
We agreed on a re-test back in July and it has not happened. It is over a month late now.

Book it this week. Everything is waiting on it. Your sessions are capped at 60 minutes because of it, and it is the reason your protein powder is gone. Until we see those numbers we are guessing.

Keep the water high and the sugar down in the meantime, same as before.

cards.title: Heavy Is the Point Now
cards.body:
Everything changes shape this cycle. Six to eight reps instead of twelve to fifteen, and two to two and a half minutes rest instead of sixty seconds. Fewer exercises, more weight on each.

When you are eating less, heavy lifting is what tells your body to keep the muscle. Light and fast does not send that message. That is the whole reason the programme looks like this.

One thing from last cycle. You sat on 35 kg on the hack squat for three weeks at an effort of 7 when the target was 8. If a set feels easier than the target, the next set goes up. Do not wait for permission.

cards.title: Your Knee Is Cleared
cards.body:
Five weeks of leg work, zero knee pain. That problem is behind you and I am not going to keep tiptoeing around it.

Single-leg work comes back this cycle as the dumbbell split squat, both feet on the floor. This is not the Bulgarian version that gave you trouble in July, and we are not going back to that one yet.

Keep the effort easy for the first two weeks. If anything sharp shows up, stop that exercise and message me. Normal muscle burn and next-day soreness are fine and expected.

cards.title: You Were Right About the Muscle
cards.body:
You said you feel a lot stronger and that you gained muscle. You did, and here it is in numbers from your own logs.

  • Hack squat up 50%
  • Shoulder press up 27%
  • Leg press up 22% in five weeks
  • Lat pulldown up 21% after a six-week plateau that would not move

And you did that training three or four days a week instead of four, in the middle of summer. That is a good cycle. Now we keep all of it while the weight comes down.

cards.title: Walking Is Your Fat Loss
cards.body:
You do not enjoy conditioning, so I have taken the circuits and the bike intervals out. No arguments from me.

What is left is the incline treadmill walk. Steep incline, easy pace, no holding the handrails. Twenty minutes on Day 4, and as often as you like on the days you are not in the gym.

It burns real calories, it does nothing to your recovery, and your legs will still be fresh for the heavy days. This is the part that moves the scale. The lifting is what keeps the muscle while it does.

cards.title: If It Is Not Logged It Did Not Happen
cards.body:
The app closed on you twice last cycle and both sessions lost their numbers. I am getting that looked at. If it happens again, message me the weights straight away so nothing goes missing.

Two things I need from you every week:

  • Your weight, same morning, same conditions, before you eat.
  • Every set logged, honestly, including the ones that felt bad.

I cannot see you train. The log is how I coach you.
